subject.title: fix: order ambient transcript watermarks by decimal ids

question: For equal-timestamp entries whose IDs are opaque or mixed with decimal IDs, should OpenClaw define lexical ordering as the durable watermark order, or treat those IDs as unordered and use a different channel-provided sequencing rule?
rationale: The patch makes a durable message-delivery and session-state policy choice that cannot be proven from unit examples alone because opaque ID ordering is owned by the upstream channel contract.

options.title: Require a channel sequencing contract
options.body: Use numeric comparison only where the channel guarantees canonical decimal IDs and define a separate authoritative ordering source or safe unordered behavior for other IDs.

options.title: Adopt lexical ordering
options.body: Document lexical ordering as the OpenClaw watermark contract and accept that channels with non-lexical opaque IDs may need an owner-specific migration or limitation.

recommendation.title: Require a channel sequencing contract
recommendation.body: Use numeric comparison only where the channel guarantees canonical decimal IDs and define a separate authoritative ordering source or safe unordered behavior for other IDs.
